What is matter? *Music* Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. We have three states of matter. They are solids, liquids and gases. The three states of matter include solids, liquids and gases. Learner, what is the difference between floating and sinking? We have looked at different solids that float and sink in water, what is the difference between floating and sinking? *Music* The objects that remain at the surface of water are floating. The objects that remain at the surface of water are floating. While those that go to the bottom of the water are sinking. Those solids that go to the bottom of the water are sinking. Materials that sink are called sinkers while the materials that float are called floaters. Can you name examples of solids that float on water? Learner, name two floaters. *Music* Solids that float on water or those that remain on the surface of the water include a paper, a pencil, a leaf and many others. A paper, a pencil and a leaf are called floaters because they float on water. Now name the solids that sink in water. Learner name two sinkers. *Music* Solids that sink in water include stone, key, coin and many others, and therefore a stone, a key and a coin are called sinkers because they sink or they go at the bottom of the water. Learner, have you asked yourself why some object sink while others float on water? Why do we have sinkers and floaters? Objects float or sink according to a number of reasons. These reasons are known as factors. Today I want us to look at the factors or the reasons that affect floating and sinking. I want us to look at the factors or reasons that affect floating and sinking. Do you have your basin that is half filled with water? And the solids, the two bottle tops?

We want to see this factors that affect floating and sinking. *Music* Let us put together the two bottle tops in the basin that is half filled with water. Remember one bottle top is normal, it is flat while the one is crushed. Learner, what do you notice? *Music* The normal flat bottle top floats on water while the crushed bottle top sinks in water. What did we do to the bottle top to make it sink? *Music* Learner, all this are bottle tops but one is floating while the other one is sinking. What did we do to the bottle top to make it sink? We crushed the bottle top and it sunk in water. A normal bottle top floats on water. Once we changed its shape it sunk in water. Therefore, shape is one of the factors or reasons that affect floating and sinking. We have different solids that float or sink in water. However, once we change their shape, then it will affect their floating or sinking. Once we change their shape it will affect their floating or sinking. Look at a ship, a ship is made of metal or steel. Do metals float or sink in water? *Music* Metals sink in water but a ship floats on water. Metals sink in water but a ship floats on water. Learner, can you tell me why a ship floats on water? *Music* A ship floats on water because it has a hollow shape. Once again shape is a factor that affects floating and sinking. Metals sink in water but a ship which is made of metal floats on water this is because it has a hollow shape. Now let us try and put the piece of wood and the piece of metal in water, which one floats and which one sinks? *Music* A piece of wood floats on water while a piece of metal sinks in water. What makes a piece of wood float on water yet a metal sinks in water ? Is it the shape? *Music*

4 ” to allow audio playback Did you say Shape? No it is not the shape. There is another factor or reason that affects floating and sinking of an item . The answer is material . The material is the reason why a piece of wood floated in water while a piece of metal sank in water. The type of material affects floating and sinking. The type of material affects floating and sinking. Materials such as paper and wood floats on water while those made of metal and steel sink in water. Therefore, material is another factor that affects floating and sinking. Now finally let us get the short and the long pencil. Let us put the short and the long pencil in water. *Music* Which one floats and which one sinks? Answer when you hear the music . *Music* I hope you have put the two pencils in water. What have you realised? *Music* Both pencils float on water. A short pencil and a long pencil float on water. Learner, which factor of floating and sinking were we looking at ? *Music* When we test a short and a long pencil, we are looking at their size. The size of a material DOES NOT affect floating and sinking. The size of a material DOES NOT affect floating and sinking. We have now seen three factors or reasons that affect floating and sinking. Now learner name three reasons that affect floating and sinking. Do that when the music begins. *Music* Good. I hope you were able to answer. I have said the following reasons will affect floating and sinking: The shape The material and The size. When you change a shape of an object, it will affect whether the object will sink or float. Size will not affect a material, whether short or long if it sinks then it sinks and if it floats then it floats. However, the type of material will make the object to float or sink in water. For your task or activity at home, find other factors that affect floating and sinking. With that learner, we have come to the end of our Science and Technology lesson for today. Goodbye.
